verdict: Spend is live but performance is invisible — no lead tracking means you cannot tell if this campaign is working.
diagnosis: This period shows $2,111 spent and 295,796 impressions on one Facebook campaign, but zero lead or conversion data to judge return.

signals.headline: Single campaign carrying $2,111 spend
signals.detail: One PCOS and postpartum persona campaign absorbs all paid budget this period. No diversification, no fallback if it fatigues.

signals.headline: 295,796 impressions delivered this period
signals.detail: Reach is meaningful for a niche persona play. Without lead data, we cannot say if impressions converted to inquiries.

signals.headline: Zero lead or conversion data reported
signals.detail: No cost per lead, no pipeline signal, no top performers. This is the biggest gap in the account right now.

signals.headline: Daily spend averaging around $75
signals.detail: Sits at the low end of the recommended fitness studio starting budget. Enough to learn, tight to scale.

signals.headline: No organic, local, or CRM signal
signals.detail: Google Business Profile, social, and pipeline data are all missing. Paid is running without any supporting context.

recommendations.title: Turn on lead tracking before adding another dollar
recommendations.detail: Consider installing Meta lead form tracking or a landing page pixel this week. Without a cost per lead number, every optimization decision is a guess.

recommendations.title: Test a second campaign to reduce single-point risk
recommendations.detail: Worth exploring a second angle — a Pilates or low-impact class hook — to complement the PCOS and postpartum persona. Protects you if fatigue hits.

recommendations.title: Prepare for July cost inflation with a low-barrier offer
recommendations.detail: Test a free week pass or $1 first-month trial. These low-friction offers help fitness studios hold cost per lead down during the July peak.
